items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Earl was a pianist called Nappy, and I had met him during my first few months at the Savoy when he had a relief band there.

ctx.x: There was not much booking after the Apollo date, but the band rehearsed once a week anyway. One day, we were rehearsing in the hall next door to the Lafayette theatre and suddenly, Sy stopped the rehearsal and started to make a speech about something. Then after, he started to ask the musicians what they thought of him? Different ones said this and that, but not all of us said what we though except Ernie Powell. Ernie had been in the army with Sy who was a sergent and was director of an army band in which Ernie…

I had a few gigs now and then which were mostly then and was getting behind in my rent. But the Normans never bothered me about that and sometimes, I would borrow a few dollars from them because they knew that When I made a gig, I would pay my rent and give back the money I had borrowed. Earl Norman, my landlord and I had built a large table in his basement on which we were going to realize our dream of havin' some miniature electric trains. Earl was an automobile mechanic and a damn good one. He also knew many…

I told Norman that, and then he says that Earle Howard was the head red cap at the Pennsylvannia railroad station and asked me why didn't get a job carrying bags. He told me that in a very polite way and I told him very politely that I didn't like to carry my own bags and had no eyes for carrying those of other people. Many New York musicians had done it, but for the time being, I figured to make it in the music game, even if there was not much on the rail for the lizard.
